targets.self_route_verdict: MISNAMED -- not a substrate readiness/convergence issue. It is an experiment-script API-misuse bug: the script's deliberate random-action rollout never calls agent.act()/act_with_split_obs()/act_with_log_prob(), and REEAgent._e1_tick() -- the only place that appends to self._world_experience_buffer -- is called exclusively from those three methods (ree_core/agent.py:8208/8238/8260). compute_prediction_loss() hard-returns a zero-gradient stub tensor whenever len(self._world_experience_buffer) < 2 (ree_core/agent.py:8556), so E1 is structurally never ticked and never trained for the entire run, on any arm, any seed.
targets.failed_criterion_detail: All three P0 readiness preconditions (world_model_converged_phaseA_control, regime_change_disconfirms_control, pe_precision_manipulation_took) measured exactly 0.0 against thresholds 0.25/1.15/1.5. arm_results confirm phaseA_episode_means and phaseB_episode_means are literally [0.0, 0.0, ...] for every episode, every seed, both metrics -- not a near-zero convergence failure but a structurally pinned zero from episode 1. The script's own degeneracy check (criteria_non_degenerate.C1=false) correctly caught this and self-routed to FAIL rather than reporting a false PASS or false negative -- no scientific harm was done, but the self-route label misattributes the cause to substrate immaturity.

targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-826 (2026-07-26, first experimental test of MECH-244) self-routed substrate_not_ready_requeue but produced no interpretable signal on the claim: E1 never received a training gradient because the script's random-action rollout never calls agent.act*() -- the only path that ticks E1 and populates the experience buffer compute_prediction_loss() reads (ree_core/agent.py:8556, 8208/8238/8260). All three P0 readiness metrics and both C1 delta arrays are structurally pinned at exactly 0.0 from episode 1, confirming a wiring bug rather than a genuine convergence failure. MECH-244 remains untested (exp_conf=0.0); route to /queue-experiment for a same-question redesign (V3-EXQ-826a) that explicitly ticks E1 (e.g. call agent._e1_tick(latent) after agent.sense(), mirroring the pattern already used correctly in V3-EXQ-822a) while preserving the random-action design (no policy confound). Also flag for follow-on: the precedent scripts this design cited for its sense()+compute_prediction_loss() API usage (v3_exq_032/032b/032c, v3_exq_396a) show the identical sense()-then-compute_prediction_loss() pattern under random-action rollout and may share the same silent zero-E1-loss defect -- worth a dedicated audit, out of scope for this autopsy.

re_derive_brake.not_fired_reason: MECH-244 has 0 prior autopsies of any kind (this is its first experimental test) and this reading is measurement_gap, not substrate_ceiling.

learning_extracted: compute_prediction_loss() silently returns a zero-gradient stub whenever the world-experience buffer has <2 entries, and that buffer is populated ONLY inside _e1_tick(), which only fires from agent.act()/act_with_split_obs()/act_with_log_prob(). Any experiment combining pure random-action rollout (bypassing all three act* methods) with E1 training via compute_prediction_loss() will silently and deterministically never train E1 -- the self-consistency check (C1 degeneracy) is what catches it, not the API.
The self-route label substrate_not_ready_requeue is a misnomer here (mirrors the V3-EXQ-642 canonical case): the substrate (E1 itself) is fine; the experiment script's driving loop never engaged it.

The 'established V3-EXQ-818 convention' of random-action rollout to remove policy confounds is incompatible with training E1 via compute_prediction_loss() as currently wired -- any future script following that convention for E1 training needs to explicitly tick E1 (e.g. via agent._e1_tick(latent), as V3-EXQ-822a already does correctly) rather than relying on sense() alone.

The same sense()+compute_prediction_loss()-under-random-rollout pattern appears in the precedent scripts this design cited (v3_exq_032 family, v3_exq_396a) -- unverified whether they share the defect; flagged as follow-on, not confirmed here.

targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-817a (2026-07-26, redesigned successor to V3-EXQ-817) demonstrates that a dedicated consequence-grounding objective CAN make the action-object space O state-dependent and consequence-structured (r2 0.98->0.72, clean paired and shuffled controls, content-vs-traffic discriminated) -- resolving V3-EXQ-817's competence_implementation_gap. But grounding this representation produced NO behavioural benefit (harm_rate flat/nominally worse across ARM_0/1/2), demoting SD-004's specific rationale that this compressed representation drives measurably better long-horizon planning/harm-avoidance. SD-080 stays candidate: this run is a correctness-not-capability finding about the DEFAULT (unmodified) substrate SD-080 describes -- 817a's objective is itself a bespoke addition, not evidence that an existing REE path already grounds O, so SD-080's 'zero gradient from every REE path' framing is not falsified by this run, though the claim's language may need updating to acknowledge grounding is achievable in principle.

re_derive_brake.not_fired_reason: Neither SD-004 nor SD-080 has any prior substrate_ceiling autopsy; this reading is standard/mixed, not a ceiling reading.

learning_extracted: The delta-prediction grounding objective that failed in V3-EXQ-817 (predicting z_world delta, which only moved the head without inducing state-dependence) was successfully replaced by a state-dependence-targeted objective in 817a -- confirms the 817 autopsy's diagnosis that the OBJECTIVE, not the substrate, was the blocker.

Achieving a consequence-structured, state-dependent O does not by itself produce a behavioural benefit in this harness -- the planner-side coupling from representation quality to action choice is a separate, still-open question, worth its own falsifier if SD-004's efficiency rationale is to be tested fairly.

SD-080 and SD-004 should be scored on different directions from the same run -- treating this as a blanket weakens on both would conflate a claim about the unmodified substrate (SD-080) with a claim about behavioural consequence (SD-004).

targets.self_route_verdict: The manifest's own note is honest and correctly scoped ('Not a verdict on INV-091'), but the label undersells a specific, traceable design confound rather than a generic readiness gap.
targets.failed_criterion_detail: Pre-registered order: similarity(decouple) < similarity(intact) < similarity(lockstep). Measured: decouple=0.2262, intact=0.2715, lockstep=0.1679. First inequality holds (decouple < intact). Second inequality is REVERSED: lockstep (0.168) is the LOWEST of all three arms, not the highest -- not a null result but a directional reversal on the lockstep leg specifically.

four_layer_diagnosis.claim_alignment: unclear -- per the script's own non-degeneracy guard, the manipulation did not test the pre-registered hypothesis; INV-091 itself is neither supported nor weakened.
four_layer_diagnosis.biological_reference: clear -- forcing synchronous cross-stream update cadence as an operationalisation of 'lockstep' coupling is a reasonable design intent (collapsed inter-stream asynchrony predicts higher similarity).
four_layer_diagnosis.prerequisites: present -- decoupling (scrambling) worked as expected on its own leg; only the lockstep leg misbehaved.
four_layer_diagnosis.implementation: traced to _force_lockstep() (script:261-265): sets e1_steps_per_tick=e2_steps_per_tick=e3_base_steps=e3_current_steps=1 -- collapsing ALL three streams to update every single environment step. Under 'intact', E3 only ticks once per 10 env-steps by default. This changes not only phase-alignment (the intended manipulation) but also the TICK SAMPLING DENSITY/RESOLUTION of every stream relative to intact, and the similarity statistic (_cross_stream_xcorr) operates in TICK units with max_lag_ticks=8 -- so a lag of '8 ticks' represents very different amounts of real elapsed time under lockstep vs intact. This is a plausible confound: the manipulation bundles synchrony together with a change in effective sampling resolution, and the two may pull the correlation statistic in opposite directions.
four_layer_diagnosis.environment: adequate for the decouple/intact contrast; the lockstep arm's clock-rate collapse is itself the confound under suspicion.
four_layer_diagnosis.measurement: the xcorr statistic and its tick-unit lag window were not designed to be invariant to a change in per-stream tick rate -- a design gap in the DV, not an instrumentation bug (the measured numbers are presumably correct given what was fed to them).
four_layer_diagnosis.scale: 1 seed reported in this pending-review row (seed[0] per the docstring's calibration note; check full per-seed detail before finalising, not required for this autopsy's routing).

biological_reference.closest_mechanism: cross-stream temporal binding / phase-coupling between distinct processing streams (e.g. thalamocortical synchrony) as a substrate for felt unity/self-world integration -- INV-091's emergent-invariant framing.
dependencies: a way to manipulate synchrony independent of sampling resolution -- not cleanly available via the current clock-rate lever
biological_reference.divergence: none identified in the underlying biological framing; the gap is in the experimental operationalisation of 'lockstep', which conflates phase-alignment with tick-rate/sampling-density.
biological_reference.lit_status: n/a (INV-091 is an emergent invariant derived from ARC-025/MECH-063/MECH-069/SD-010/SD-011/MECH-035, not a single literature-grounded claim)

targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-827 (2026-07-26) failed its own pre-registered non-degeneracy guard: the lockstep arm produced the LOWEST cross-stream similarity of the three arms (0.168), reversing rather than merely nulling the predicted decouple<intact<lockstep order (decouple 0.226 < intact 0.271 held; lockstep did not exceed intact). Traced to _force_lockstep() collapsing e1/e2/e3 tick rates to 1, which changes tick sampling density/resolution alongside phase-alignment -- a likely confound given the similarity statistic (_cross_stream_xcorr) operates in tick-unit lags (max_lag_ticks=8) that represent very different real time under lockstep vs intact's default ~10-env-step E3 cadence. Per the script's own guard, this is 'not a verdict on INV-091'. Route to /queue-experiment for a same-question redesign (V3-EXQ-827a) that forces phase-synchrony without altering per-stream tick rate/sampling density (e.g. align tick BOUNDARIES across streams while preserving each stream's own native rate), and/or normalizes the cross-correlation window to real elapsed time rather than raw tick count so cross-arm comparisons are on a common temporal scale.

re_derive_brake.not_fired_reason: INV-091 has 0 prior autopsies; this is its first test and the reading is measurement_test_design_defect, not substrate_ceiling.

learning_extracted: The decouple leg of the design (iei_permute landmark scrambling) worked exactly as intended (decouple < intact held) -- the design's problem is isolated to the lockstep leg's clock-rate manipulation, not the whole apparatus.

Forcing synchrony via a uniform tick-rate-of-1 collapse conflates phase-alignment with sampling-density/resolution; any INV-091 redesign needs a synchrony lever that is orthogonal to tick rate, or a similarity statistic normalized to real elapsed time rather than raw tick count.

A directional REVERSAL (not just a null) on one specific arm, while the other arm's leg of the same guard behaved as predicted, is itself diagnostic -- it points at that arm's specific manipulation rather than a generic power/measurement problem across the whole design.
